title: Adaptive Inference Economics Initiative: Real-time Prefetch + Quant Signal Trials
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Run a coordinated set of experiments that combine adaptive prefetch (prefix-aware KV caching), dynamic batching policy adjustments, and lightweight per-request quantization signals to reduce hosted per-token cost while holding user-facing latency and quality SLOs.

Hypothesis: By surfacing a low-cost inference signal for common request shapes (short-turn chat, system prompts with heavy prefix reuse) and routing those to quantized / cached fast paths we can achieve 12–20% aggregate token cost reduction for mid-tail workloads with <5% regression in generation quality and latency within our P99 SLO.

Scope: 1) Design and validate a runtime signal that tags requests suitable for quantized kernels (loss-aware proxy), 2) Prefetch and pin KV entries for high-volume prompt prefixes, 3) Adaptive batch-size tuning to preserve latency SLOs during bursts, 4) Monitor quality regressions via prompt-set evals and automatic rollback.

Deliverables: Experiment plan and criteria doc (Confluence), telemetry dashboards (Console route + per-model cost breakdown), canary rollout automation, A/B analysis notebook, runbook for abort/rollback and customer comms template. Links: https://confluence.redwood/internal/adaptive-econ, PR template: https://github.com/redwood-infr/adaptive-econ/pulls

Risks & Mitigations: Potential quality regressions from quantized routing -> gate by per-prompt eval buckets and delta thresholds; Unexpected latency spikes due to prefetch saturation -> implement backpressure and conservative prefetch caps; Misclassification of 'cheap' requests -> start with conservative classifier, expand cohorts after safety windows.

Stakeholders: PM (Maya Chen), Eng leads (Ravi Singh, Noor Patel), Research (Dr. Elena Park), Design (Jon Ruiz), SRE (Liam O'Connor).
metrics: Primary: token cost reduction vs baseline (percent)
Quality: BLEU/ROUGE-like eval delta and human-rated sample pass rate (%)
Operational: rollback events, failed-canary rate, false-classification rate
acceptance_criteria: Experiment run completed on representative traffic for two weeks with stable telemetry
>=12% reduction in per-token cost on targeted cohort OR clear roadmap to achieve it with incremental changes
Quality regression <=5% on automated evals and <2% human-failure rate
Automated rollback executes within 5 minutes on metric-triggered alert
